name: World.create() async factory + repository-backed populateNamespace
summary: Make World construction go through an async factory that eagerly populates the namespace via repository.findMany(), instead of lazily via direct fs calls. Fixes a layering leak where World assumes FileRepository internals.

rawActions.name: Add World.create() factory (repository-based, no direct fs)
rawActions.summary: static async create(worldPath, repository = new FileRepository(worldPath), id = new UUID64()): Promise<World> in world.ts. Constructs World, then await repository.saveWorld(world) (NOT fs.writeFileSync -- must go through the repository interface, same principle as populateNamespace()), sets lastSyncTime, then await world.populateNamespace() before returning. Absorbs FileRepository.create()'s logic but routes all persistence through IEntityRepository methods -- no direct fs calls in World. The 'throw if world already exists' guard (currently fs.existsSync(worldFile)) is filesystem-specific and needs rethinking behind the repository interface (e.g. attempt loadWorld() and treat success as already-exists) rather than being ported as-is.

rawActions.name: Make populateNamespace() async, use repository.findMany()
rawActions.summary: Rewrite World.populateNamespace() (world.ts:214-269) to be async and use 'for await (const instance of this.repository.findMany(IEntity, {}))' instead of manual fs.readdirSync/readFileSync/UUID64.fromString reconstruction. Mirrors FileRepository#load() (file-repository.ts:64-82). Note: old per-file try/catch that skipped malformed JSON is dropped (YAGNI, untested) -- a bad file now propagates and halts population.

rawActions.name: Resolve async populateNamespace vs sync namespace getters
rawActions.summary: populateNamespace() becoming async conflicts with the synchronous Entity.namespace/mutableNamespace getters (entity.ts:50-56, 68-74) which call it lazily. Population must happen eagerly in World.create() so #namespace is already populated before any getter runs. Investigate whether Entity.populateNamespace() can stay abstract/sync for other subclasses (e.g. Task, task.ts:91) while World special-cases eager population in its own constructor path/create().

rawActions.name: Update call sites to await World.create()
rawActions.summary: Update src/cli/cli-init.ts and src/nf-program.ts, which currently call FileRepository.create(worldPath) synchronously, to instead call 'await World.create(worldPath)'. Remove or deprecate FileRepository.create() (file-repository.ts ~303-326) once logic is absorbed into World.create().

rawActions.name: Run tests and verify
rawActions.summary: Run npm run test:unit (or npm test) from pkg/nameforma; confirm all existing tests pass, especially World construction/namespace-population tests. Add/confirm a test that World.create() returns a World whose .namespace already contains entities loaded from a pre-populated .nameforma directory (no lazy-load surprise).

rawReferences.name: Deferred: World.load(), syncRepository(), entityList() still bypass repository via raw fs
rawReferences.summary: Not in scope for this task. World.load()/FileRepository.load() need the same async-factory treatment. syncRepository() (world.ts:467-574) uses raw fs + mtime-as-updatedAt-proxy; should eventually use repository.findMany(EntityClass, {updatedAt: {$gt: syncStart}}) + repository.distinct('id', {collection}) for deletion detection. entityList() (world.ts:700-741) needs the same findMany(EntityClass, {}) replacement as populateNamespace(). Also: IEntityRepository.loadWorld() is typed Promise<Record<string,any>> (entity.ts:143) but FileRepository.loadWorld() actually returns Promise<World> -- pre-existing type looseness worth tightening.
